[h2]Resumen del Juego[/h2]
ACE Academy es básicamente una novela visual con traje de “Acción, Aventura, Rol, Simuladores y Deportes”… y sí, también con mechas, porque en el anime si no hay un robot gigante no te gradúas. Entras a una academia donde el romance, las decisiones “importantes” y el drama escolar se mezclan con combates/competencias estilo deportivo en 2D, con un enfoque clarísimo en la narración y en elegir tu propia aventura.

La primera impresión es: “Qué adorable todo… hasta que recuerdas que el juego te vendió la fantasía de acción y deportes y tú estás leyendo diálogos como si fuera examen final de literatura”. Eso sí, tiene encanto: personajes estilo anime, tono relajado, y la promesa de finales múltiples para que tu vida social digital salga mejor que la real.

Lo Bueno:
✅ 🧠 Las elecciones importan y empujan a varios finales, ideal para el síndrome de “¿y si hubiera dicho lo otro?”
✅ 💘 Romance y simulador de citas con vibra anime: cómodo, ligero y con momentos genuinamente divertidos
✅ 🤖 Mecha + academia + drama: una mezcla ridícula… o sea, perfecta para el género
✅ 🎨 2D agradable y personajes “adorables” que hacen fácil engancharse
✅ ☁️ Steam Cloud: tus decisiones cuestionables viajan contigo

Lo No Tan Bueno:
❌ 📉 0 logros: Steam no te va a aplaudir ni cuando logres el final “bueno” (ni el “por favor no”)
❌ 👥 Solo un jugador: tu vergüenza romántica es completamente en solitario

ACE Academy is a character-driven visual novel that blends slice-of-life storytelling, light science fiction, and romantic drama into a cohesive and approachable experience. Developed and published by PixelFade, the game presents itself as a school-life narrative set in a near-future world where mechanized combat robots have evolved from military tools into competitive sporting icons. Rather than focusing on large-scale conflict or dystopian themes, the game centers on personal growth, relationships, and the challenge of finding one’s place in an unfamiliar environment, giving it a grounded and relatable emotional core despite its futuristic setting.

The story follows a transfer student arriving at the prestigious ACE Academy, an institution dedicated to training pilots for competitive GEAR combat. From the beginning, the protagonist is positioned as an outsider, burdened by past setbacks and stuck with outdated equipment that immediately marks him as different from his peers. This sense of displacement drives much of the early narrative, as the player navigates social awkwardness, team dynamics, and the pressure to prove themselves in a highly competitive academic culture. The academy setting serves as both a literal and symbolic arena, where personal confidence, trust, and teamwork are just as important as technical skill.

The game’s greatest strength lies in its cast of characters and the way interactions are handled. Each major character is distinct, with their own motivations, insecurities, and interpersonal conflicts, and the writing does a strong job of balancing humor with sincerity. Dialogue choices allow players to shape how relationships develop, influencing friendships and potential romantic paths in ways that feel meaningful rather than purely cosmetic. While the overall plot follows a linear structure, these branching interactions give the experience replay value and encourage players to explore different emotional outcomes.

Romance routes are integrated naturally into the narrative rather than existing as isolated side content. Emotional connections develop gradually through shared experiences, conversations, and moments of vulnerability, making the romantic arcs feel earned. Even outside of romance, the game places significant emphasis on friendship and teamwork, reinforcing the idea that success at the academy is not an individual pursuit. This focus helps maintain narrative cohesion and prevents the story from feeling like a collection of disconnected character routes.

Presentation is another area where ACE Academy stands out, especially considering it was PixelFade’s debut title. Character artwork is clean and expressive, rendered in high resolution with attention to subtle facial expressions that enhance emotional scenes. The inclusion of full English voice acting adds depth to the dialogue and helps bring the characters to life, making interactions feel more personal and engaging. The soundtrack supports the tone well, shifting between upbeat tracks for school-life moments and more subdued compositions during reflective or dramatic scenes without ever overpowering the narrative.

That said, the game is not without its shortcomings. Pacing can feel uneven, particularly in the latter portion of the story, where certain plot threads resolve more quickly than expected. Some players may find the conclusion less satisfying than the buildup, as the ending can feel abrupt or open-ended depending on the route taken. These issues do not undermine the overall experience, but they do highlight the game’s nature as an early work, where ambition occasionally outpaces execution.

From a gameplay perspective, ACE Academy adheres closely to traditional visual novel conventions. There are no complex systems or mini-games beyond dialogue choices, and progression depends entirely on reading, decision-making, and managing save points to explore alternate paths. For fans of the genre, this simplicity is a strength, allowing the focus to remain on story and character development. Players looking for more mechanical variety, however, may find the interactivity limited.

Overall, ACE Academy succeeds as a heartfelt and polished visual novel that emphasizes character relationships, personal growth, and the quiet drama of everyday life within a futuristic setting. While it may not redefine the genre or deliver a perfectly paced narrative, it offers a warm, engaging experience that resonates through its writing and cast. As both a standalone title and a foundation for PixelFade’s later works, it remains a solid and enjoyable entry for players who appreciate story-driven games with romance, humor, and a strong sense of character focus.

ACE Academy is a very well made dating sim visual novel that feels like a lot of love went into it. This is probably one of the few true high quality western produced dating sims.

The game takes place in a futuristic school environment with mechas, and you build your relationship with multiple female classmates. Although the overarching story is nothing too exciting and mostly linear, the choices are actually meaningful for the relationships/certain events. The dialogue is pretty well written, and you can tell the writers knew what they were doing. There are plenty of witty remarks, references, and a more "western" tinge for some writing/humor (vs japanese style writing). The game is also fully voice acted (English only though), and I think the VAs really did a great job. I especially liked Valerie and Shou's VAs. All the art/character portraits were also very well made, and the music was very solid. The only gripe I have with the game is that the ending felt like it was a bit rushed, and we didn't see a more satisfying resolution for an overhanging plot point.

Overall, solid dating sim that grew on me more and more as I played it. I would recommend the game to anyone who likes dating sims, and I look forward to playing the other games by PixelFade.

If you play ACE Academy focusing only on the main story without getting into the romances, it's honestly pretty mid. The plot alone isn't strong enough to carry the game, and the ending... well... what ending? Nothing to write home about.

But it gets significantly better if you start messing around with people. Choosing the funny options and just enjoying the banter. The characters become more entertaining, and the experience overall feels more engaging and fun.

Where ACE Academy really shines to me is in its romance. The character arcs are completely missiable if you’re not focusing on them, but if you do engage with them, they can be surprisingly heartfelt and rewarding. 

That said, not all the routes are created equal. It’s pretty clear to me that one girl got the developer’s full attention, with significantly more depth and polish than some of the others. It doesn’t ruin the experience, but it does make some of the other routes feel a bit underwhelming in comparison. Or it could just be me being biased. 

Also, as you restart to try different routes, the game starts to feel repetitive really fast. A lot of scenes and structure are reused, so chasing every romance feels super tedious even with the skip button. 

ACE Academy has great humor, heartfelt moments, and pretty solid romance. The music is pretty good and fits the mood well, but I do wish the art quality was a bit more aesthetically pleasing. As for the ending—it didn’t really land for me. It felt like the season just stopped midway without proper closure. Still, despite its flaws, I genuinely enjoyed my time with it.

Is it the best visual novel or interactive story out there? No, not by a long shot. However, is it a fun and well-made experience? Absolutely.

The story may be fairly cheesy and filled with typical manga/anime romance tropes, with a touch of sci-fi mech added for good measure. Its still a resalable story in its genre. You'll encounter all the classic stereotypes, from the goofball to the super shy girl, and more.

The visuals, while not the most breathtaking, are perfectly adequate for the style chosen and contribute to the overall charm of the game.

One of the standout features is the plethora of choices available to the player. While it's not always clear how these choices impact the story beyond affecting a hidden metric of how much an NPC likes you, it still add a fun layer of engagement that keeps the experience fresh.

Do I recommend this game? Yes, definitely. It's a delightful experience for fans of visual novels, dating sims, and/or manga-inspired games. If you're new to this genre and want to see if it's for you, this game serves as an excellent starting point. It's easy to grasp, and you won't need to overthink every decision or manage a plethora of details.
Overall, it's a light, enjoyable adventure that provides just the right amount of fun without overwhelming the player.

ACE Academy is a game that has potential, but it falls short of my expectations.

Having recently played visual novels from well-established Japanese developers, I found myself comparing ACE Academy to them. It's perhaps unfair to draw direct comparisons, considering one was made by an indie dev team backed through Kickstarter, while the other... well, you know.

Reused backgrounds are my biggest issue with this VN. It's one of the few things that truly pulls me out of being immersed in a VN. I usually imagine entire worlds around the backgrounds and location descriptions, but it gets completely thrown off by reusing them. I'd honestly prefer they simply showed me the sky than reuse backgrounds. 
Another issue is the seemingly odd choice of story placement. Throughout the entire game, you get to pick who you want to have interactions with. I'd been avoiding picking Mayu the entire time until I couldn't anymore. An entire backstory of how the MC and Mayu started a band and were looking for a singer. I'm sorry, what? This is the first I've heard of this, and it's never brought up again either. Perhaps it's featured in the Mayu route, but I can't be bothered to read her route, to be honest. 
This is something that the game does quite a bit where it springs onto you little bits of story that don't really quite make sense. I'm not a writer so I couldn't quite put my finger on it, but for some of them, something just felt off every so often.

Now that I've got my peeves out of the way, I want to say something positive. I can tell there was a lot of passion behind this project; I actually burst out into a full-on laugh several times, and not many games can do that. 
The voice actors did a great job, and it was nice listening to English voices for once. 
The art has its charm to it, and I think it works rather well. 
While the story isn't the best thing I've read, it's nicely executed and wraps up alright. While I would've liked to see it fleshed out more, the devs simply didn't have that privilege with the funds.

So in short, I didn't love ACE Academy, but I had fun. There are improvements to be made. I look forward to playing what they've brought out since they released this.

Přiznám se - hned po dohrání Crystalline (další skvělá vizuální novela, moje recenze [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/artemiscze/recommended/616250/]ZDE[/url]) jsem nadšeně koupil i zbytek vizuálních novel od studia PixelFade, jelikož po důkladném přečtení mnoha recenzí mi bylo jasné, že celá jejich tvorba je stejně kvalitní jako právě Crystalline. No a řekl jsem si, proč to nevzít od úplného začátku a nezahrát si jejich úplně první novelu. Dámy a pánové, vítejte v ACE Academy!

Příběh se odehrává v blízké budoucnosti roku 2049, kdy světem hýbou zápasy obrovských mechů, kterým se říká GEAR. Ujmete se role amerického pilota GEARu, který se čerstvě přestěhoval do Japonska, aby zde mohl navštěvovat prestižní školu pro GEAR piloty - ACE Academy. Hned na začátku má hlavní hrdina problém se začleněním do kolektivu, jelikož díky jeho zastaralému americkému mechovi ho nechce do svých řad žádný kompetetivní tým. Až do chvíle, kdy se na poli objeví tým, který opravdu nutně potřebuje nového člena - což je perfektní příležitost pro našeho hrdinu!

A přesně v tu chvílí začíná naše cesta za vítězstvím v šampionátu (a taky za získáním srdce jedné z dívek ;). Oproti Crystalline se jedná o více typickou novelu v tom smyslu, že zde je na výběr z několika dívek, o které se můžete ucházet, resp. "cest" kterými se můžete vydat. Opět jsou tu volby, kdy máte mnohdy na výběr co říct nebo jak se zachovat. Jedná se o bezvadný způsob, jak se do příběhu i postav mnohem víc vcítit a zároveň personalizovat váš zážitek z průchodu hrou. Co se týče postav, těch je tu hned několik a jsou velmi rozličné a ze začátku i svým způsobem tajemné - každá postava skrývá víc, než se na první pohled zdá.

V interakcích s postavami se skrývá pravá síla ACE Academy. Postupně si se zbytkem týmu vybudujete silné pouto a bude vám záležet na jejich osudech a výsledcích každého zápasu. Moje nejoblíbenější momenty z celé hry jsou právě volné chvíle mezi zápasy, strávené s vašimi parťáky a spolužáky. Objevovat jejich osobní příběhy a motivace je zkrátka a dobře jedna velká radost. Jak už jsem zmínil předtím, mezi těmito postavami je i několik dívek, se kterými máte možnost během postupu hrou navázat romantický vztah.

Já jsem prošel pouze jednu cestu hrou, kdy jsem si jako svoji dívku zvolil Kaori. Zprvu jsem ji považoval naopak za poslední možnost, protože se často jevila jako arogantní a nepříjemná, ale postupem času zjistíte, že v jádru je úplně jiná a skrývá se v ní křehká lidská bytost, která myslí v první řadě na ostatní a až pak na sebe. A takhle je to s každou postavou, nikdy nesázejte na první dojem, dát šanci se zde vyplatí.

Stejně jako v případě Crystalline, i tady jsou postavy plně anglicky nadabované, což mnohým hráčům usnadní přístup k této vizuální novele. Herci opět předvedli super výkony a hlasy k postavám skvěle sedí. Styl grafiky je taky pěkný a ačkoliv prostředí nejsou tak pěkná na pohled jako tomu bylo u fantasy Terry z Crystalline, i tady se na ně krásně kouká.

Nevím, co víc dodat. Jedná se o zábavné a komediální čtení s volbami a super postavami, které umí pracovat s emocemi a i přes komediálního ducha umí být vážné, kdy je to zrovna třeba. Rozhodně doporučuji.

You play as (insert protagonist name of your choice), a university-age man that moves from the US to Japan, and enrols in the pilot program in Ace Academy (title drop). It combines themes of sci-fi, romance, and (mild) intrigue into a package. Beware of quick-time events, and play with a mouse so you can cheat your way through said QTEs by scrolling up, if you're not into that sort of thing.

The art is charming, and the character designs flattering. All of the CGs are very nice to look at, and well composed. I tip my hat to the artists.

The comedy aspects are kept in-check quite well, and don't ruin serious moments and immersion (too much), while the romance isn't so sappy, and overbearing as to dilute the rest of the game.
You're in for about 8-12 hours of content, and there is replay value to be had. I can't speak as to how dynamic the plot is, as I am just about to replay now. 
Would definitely recommend, and the only thing I'm disappointed by is how short the game is, but at the end of the day, it's a crowdfunded project.

Around 9 hours for a single playthrough. I got through each of the "routes" (Mixed/Family, Shou, Yuuna, Mayu, Valerie, Kaori) once and it came out to around 24 hours (including waiting for the already-seen dialogue to be skipped over when doing new routes.) Even after that though there are many minor choices and combinations I noticed that would most likely add special dialogues that I didn't choose.

Regarding the story expect more slice of life rather than having it be plot focused. The routes are also more just experiencing different character interactions rather than branching into different narratives. The ending finishes with almost all of the main story buildup still unanswered. If you want a good story arc this isn't the game, if you just want a slice of life mixed with a nice choose-your-own-adventure then this is pretty good. At times the dialogue options made me feel like I was playing a good old-fashioned RPG instead of a Visual Novel. The breadth of options wasn't large, but you could still have many forms of the character you control. Better than the standard black-and-white replies of other visual novels (even though the game does still do that at times).

Voice acting was about what I expected. They do fairly well especially given that they were probably not given direction for every scene. This does mean the mannerisms/tones don't always match with the context. There are some missing and or half-missing voice lines mixed in along with a couple audio design errors. The music is pretty decent and well-made.

If you are unsatisfied after a single playthrough and don't usually play through multiple routes I'd encourage you to give this one a shot. You don't have to read the whole thing over again you can use the "skip-seen-text" feature to skip to all the parts you haven't read yet. Focus on a character and enjoy the ride. I was kinda indifferent after my first read, but came to enjoy the journey more after experiencing so many options.

The second half starts to show some of the flaws of having so many choices. Implied events that didn't occur earlier because you chose differently. These continuity errors really stick out and sours the overall experience. Most of the time they at least add a few tie in lines for stuff you may have missed/to catch you up to the scenes, but not always.
 
Concerning Quality of life this game had quite a few noticeable problems and missing features. Which is understandable for what this game is and when it came out. No Fullscreen support for Win10 (there's a setting option for it, but it's bugged.) I tried some of the fixes in the steam discussions, but none worked for me so I ended up playing in windowed the whole time.
No Backlog/History/Back Button support so if you miss what a character said due to the occasional miss tap/click you will have to reload a save. It also makes skipping already seen text on future playthroughs more annoying due not being able to look at the current conversation before choosing between options.

The game does have Mobile store ports that are baseline cheaper, but Steam sales usually will make it cheaper here.
